executiveSummary: GM0824's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained centre, 33,108 residents, 35 neighbourhoods, four BAG woonplaatsen, 21 BRT settlement labels and Midden- en West-Brabant safety-region membership are coherent. Neighbourhood population is three below the municipality total (-0.009%) and can be reconciled without rewriting rounded observations. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes, but the local interpretation is not release-ready. The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset publishes 1.200688 m direct inundation and 18,056 affected resident-equivalents through T+72 without selecting a Voorste Stroom, Achterste Stroom/Reusel, Essche Stroom or downstream Dommel boundary condition, control state, defence case or inundation footprint. Eight materially different active hazard presets reuse exactly the same full 35-neighbourhood severity order. The canonical wildfire produces remote smoke but zero local flame despite the Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen/Kampina landscape and documented elevated fire phase. A controlled hypothetical source at the official centre of buitengebied Oisterwijk Zuid produces local fire but ranks its own source neighbourhood only 13th of 35. Resident-only exposure omits the municipality's estimated 500,000-800,000 annual nature-area visits and vulnerable institutional populations. N65/A58/rail/rural access, stream crossings, external acute care, RWZI Haaren, drinking water, power and telecom remain generic or context-only. Dated observations, planning projects, annual estimates, registers and missing topology are Unknown/NoData outside their stated scope, never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0824 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement input
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK snapshot retrieved 2026-08-31; BRT source date 2025-07-01
supports: CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0824 as Oisterwijk in Noord-Brabant and reports 33,108 residents, density 413/km2, 26.0% aged 65 or older and 4,913 one-person households. The generated centre [5.201673923775259, 51.55075934773902] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Thirty-five neighbourhood rows in nineteen districts sum to 33,105 residents, three below the municipality total (-0.009%); households sum to 14,590 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 8,610. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 33,108 without changing source observations.

All four active BAG woonplaatsen—Haaren, Heukelom, Moergestel and Oisterwijk—are contained. Twenty-one BRT labels independently distinguish three woonkernen, one deelkern, three gehuchten and fourteen buurtschappen. BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; the regional bundle reports CBS CC BY 4.0.

All rows contain core population, household, age, land and water fields. Home value and several housing/benefit fields cover 33/35, cars per household 30/35, GP/supermarket distance 34/35, and district heat/public charging 0/35. Missing, suppressed, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — NWB-Light, rail and scheduled-transit context consumed by the simulator
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 2026-08-31/2026-09-03; NWB and ProRail public geometry CC0 1.0
supports: Three logical border links represent A58 west to Tilburg, A58 east to Oirschot and an N65 edge to Tilburg. The two A58 series edges share physical corridor NWB-road-58 and are not parallel capacity.
Nominal capacities 260/260/150 are synthetic scenario units and route eligibility is Mobility/Supply, not measured emergency throughput or utility topology.

One ProRail station point, Oisterwijk, lies inside GM0824. Fifty-three GTFS stop areas demonstrate scheduled service to Oisterwijk, Moergestel and Haaren, not incident-time trains/buses, vehicles, timetable operation or evacuation capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Programma Water en Riolering 2023-2027 and climate-adaptation semantics
evidenceSources.edition: municipal programme 2023-2027, published 2023-08-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: The programme separates heavy-rain, groundwater nuisance, drought/low groundwater and municipal/water-board/province responsibilities. It notes that function, hydrological state, duration and affected parcels matter in deciding action.

Local rainwater facilities are preferred; the published design narrative says local facilities that cannot process more than 60 mm overflow to public storage/infiltration and then preferably surface water or otherwise combined sewerage.

Oisterwijk's current climate-adaptation page names separated rain sewers and wadis at Telstarlaan, Molenbeemd and De Tiend, while the broader programme is expected later in 2026. A design threshold or project statement is not current capacity, observed flooding or guaranteed T+72 performance.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Voorste/Achterste/Essche Stroom system, water retention and current project stages
evidenceSources.edition: current project pages accessed 2026-09-03; Essche Stroom phased works since 2005; Voorste Stroom design phase 2026-2027; reuse licence not stated
supports: The Essche Stroom begins at Oisterwijk where the Voorste and Achterste Stroom meet, then flows about twelve kilometres to the Dommel at Halder; the Rosep, Nemer and Kleine Aa join it downstream.

The water board describes former channel straightening, kades and weirs and current policy to retain water and restore meanders. Voorste Stroom planning between A65 and Laag Heukelomseweg addresses flow, water quality, groundwater and drought in the Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen.

The Voorste Stroom project was still in research/design with construction expected after a project decision in 2027. Planned measures and completed phases cannot be treated as live hydraulic capacity or scenario-time control state.

RWZI Haaren treats wastewater from Oisterwijk, Haaren and Helvoirt, has stated design capacity 60,000 population-equivalents and discharges to the Essche Stroom. Design facts are not live inflow, bypass, power, quality or restoration state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Visie Toerisme en Recreatie Oisterwijk 2022
evidenceSources.edition: strategic vision adopted/published 2022 with horizon 2030; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality estimates Kampina and Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen together attract roughly 500,000-800,000 visits annually, including an estimated 416,000 to Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen.
The same document explicitly says many facility visitor counts are unavailable, there is no central collection point and concrete domestic/foreign visitor data is insufficient.
Annual estimates establish material transient exposure but cannot be divided into event-hour occupancy, evacuation demand or affected residents. Missing incident-time counts remain Unknown, not zero.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Kampina and Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen nature and recreation context
evidenceSources.edition: current land-manager page accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: Kampina includes wet heath, fens, woodland and grassland; Oisterwijkse Bossen en Vennen has extensive forest, fens, routes, visitor facilities and hospitality. Natuurmonumenten reports drought pressure and ongoing ecological/hydrological restoration.

The nature vision distinguishes the more intensively visited Oisterwijkse forests from quieter Kampina and notes roads/recreation businesses between the areas. Current pages identify visitor centres, routes and access points.

Land-cover and visitor infrastructure are eligibility/exposure context, not a live ignition, fuel-moisture surface, perimeter, people count, road state, extinguishing-water inventory or suppression forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel and Crisisplan 2023-2027
evidenceSources.edition: adopted regional risk profile and crisis plan 2023-2027; reuse licence not stated
supports: The safety region identifies digital/vital-infrastructure disruption, extreme weather and nature fire among its five priority risks and explicitly includes relevant risks from adjacent regions.
The regional crisis plan defines who acts and informs whom, responsibilities, measures and cooperation. This governance context is absent from generic recovery curves.
A regional priority is not an incident observation, municipal probability field, resource roster or T+72 consequence.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Dated elevated nature-fire warning and response guidance
evidenceSources.edition: municipal Phase 2 notice dated 2026-06-25; dynamic national phase method checked 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: Oisterwijk documented Phase 2 after prolonged dry conditions and warned that fire could spread rapidly and unpredictably, especially with wind. Guidance was to flee toward a public road if possible, move perpendicular to fire spread, help others and report precise location to 112.
The national phase is assessed daily from weather, field observations and land-manager/fire-service information; phases can change around midnight and response deployment is region-specific.

The June notice is historical unless current authority status separately confirms it. Neither a past nor current phase is an ignition, perimeter, spread forecast, evacuation route or guaranteed response capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Oisterwijk Jonkheerpad rail/Essche Stroom crossing context
evidenceSources.edition: project completed 2024; page updated 2025-03-06; reuse licence not stated
supports: The former unprotected Jonkheerpad crossing near Kampina/Nemerlaer was closed and replaced in 2024 by a pedestrian tunnel located where the Essche Stroom passes beneath the railway.
This confirms a locally important rail-water-access intersection and visitor route. Completion does not establish flood clearance, live passability, train operation or emergency vehicle suitability.
Oisterwijk station presence and static rail geometry must not be interpreted as incident-time passenger capacity or an evacuation corridor.

evidenceSources.title: E10 — National IMWA/DAMO water-control and wastewater public-context snapshot
evidenceSources.edition: deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z; CC BY-SA 4.0; explicitly partial national aggregation
supports: Forty-nine points are assigned inside GM0824: two sewer pumps, RWZI Haaren, eight surface-water pumps and 38 weirs. Named pumps include Waterhoef, Aboomsestraat, Pannenschuur, 't Stokske, Heirbaan and Gemaal Moergestel.

Most weir capacities and several pump capacities are null; reported numeric capacity has no dependable common unit in the app. Connected catchment, live state, power dependency, redundancy and repair status are absent.
The snapshot is partial and duplicate/naming semantics require source review; an absent or null record is Unknown/NoData, never no asset or zero capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu / Koraal
evidenceSources.title: E11 — External acute-care roles and De Hondsberg specialist-care context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM questionnaire version 1.1 published 2026-07-03, retrieved 2026-09-02, CC0 1.0; Koraal current location page accessed 2026-09-03, reuse licence not stated
supports: No registered acute-care department lies inside GM0824. Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis Tilburg is approximately 6.903 km straight-line from the municipality reference point; Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis is approximately 15.783 km.

Koraal identifies De Hondsberg in Oisterwijk as a specialist child/youth observation, diagnostics and treatment location with intensive support and residential forms, including a national 24-hour-care function.

Facility identity and straight-line distance do not establish current clients, dependency, evacuation/shelter policy, staffing, beds, power backup, route passability, hospital acceptance or incident capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E12 — Oisterwijk drinking-water sources and dated electricity/gas operational context
evidenceSources.edition: Brabant Water rolling current-year quality context; Enexis live municipality page checked 2026-09-03; reuse licences not stated
supports: Brabant Water identifies Haaren and Oirschot as Oisterwijk's drinking-water production sources and says linked quality reports are rolling current-year reports updated quarterly.

At access, Enexis reported no current Oisterwijk gas or power outage, a cancelled future interruption for postcode 5061AC and one resolved 2026-08-29 outage. Its project page reports the Oisterwijk medium-voltage network currently full and a George Perklaan reinforcement planned from September 2026.

A current no-outage page is a timestamped observation only, not zero hazard or T+72 continuity. Quality reports and planning congestion do not reveal pipe/feeder topology, live load, reserve, emergency power, damage, switching or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E13 — Denk vooruit: first-72-hour preparedness and planned emergency support points
evidenceSources.edition: current municipal preparedness page accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality tells residents to prepare for the first 72 hours with a household emergency kit/plan, information channels and mutual support; it highlights prolonged power, drinking-water and internet failure.
The municipality says it is preparing emergency support points, works with VRMWB and gives extra attention to vulnerable residents.
Preparedness advice and an intention to prepare support points do not prove household compliance, selected sites, opening, staffing, supplies, accessibility, communications or incident-time capacity.

identity.summary: GM0824, Oisterwijk, Noord-Brabant and safety region Midden- en West-Brabant agree across the consumed official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature id, bundle code and bundle name match; the safety-region assignment is unique.
Identity verification does not establish hazard, asset or service calibration.

geography.summary: The official 2025 generalized polygon and generated reference point are internally coherent.
notes: The audit context reports centre [5.201673923775259, 51.55075934773902] inside the boundary.
Administrative containment does not encode Voorste/Achterste/Essche Stroom hydraulics, groundwater, terrain, vens, forest fuels, recreation occupancy, rail-water crossings or an incident footprint.

demography.summary: Municipality and neighbourhood population totals reconcile within CBS small-area rounding.
notes: Municipality population is 33,108; 35 neighbourhoods sum to 33,105, a three-person difference (-0.009%).
Age 65+ is 26.0% and 4,913 one-person households matter for assistance demand, not automatic restoration priority.
Resident totals omit event-time visitors and do not identify institutional clients. Annual nature visits and De Hondsberg roles cannot be converted to live occupancy.

regionalDetail.summary: All 35 neighbourhoods and 36 fields are represented, but material fields, transient exposure and institution continuity remain incomplete.
notes: Cars per household covers 30/35; home value and several housing/benefit fields 33/35; GP/supermarket distance 34/35; district heat/public charging 0/35.
Dorp Haaren is the largest row at 4,755, followed by Pannenschuur Centrum 3,560 and Waterhoef 2,610. Forest, bungalow, industrial and dispersed rural rows remain separately visible.
Visitor estimates, school use and care roles are not resident-equivalent values. Missing current people, accessibility and resource state remain Unknown.

settlements.summary: Four BAG woonplaatsen and 21 BRT settlement polygons are assigned without generalized-boundary leakage.
notes: BAG covers Haaren, Heukelom, Moergestel and Oisterwijk; BRT independently distinguishes 14 buurtschappen, three gehuchten, three woonkernen and one deelkern.
Settlement population metadata is descriptive and is not forced to reconcile with CBS residents.

transport.summary: Official A58/N65/rail identities are useful, but three border links omit internal roads, crossings, live rail/road operation and evacuation capacity.
notes: Two A58 links are consecutive series edges on one physical corridor; the 0.142 km N65 border proxy captures geometry only. N65 dependence extends beyond the modeled edge and cannot be inferred from its nominal 150 units.
Oisterwijk station and 53 GTFS stops are not live service. The rail/Essche Stroom Jonkheerpad tunnel is pedestrian infrastructure, not an emergency-vehicle crossing or guaranteed dry route.
Internal rural/forest roads, bridges/culverts, fire/water passability, station operation, rolling stock, substitute buses and Tilburg-hospital routing are absent.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative risk, water, nature, care and preparedness context exists, but live roles, resources and first-72-hour decisions are not represented.
notes: VRMWB prioritizes extreme weather, nature fire and vital/digital disruption; Oisterwijk documents first-72-hour self-preparation and planned support points.

The simulator has no selected water event/control state, ignition/perimeter, fire-weather validity, live visitor/institution count, road/rail closure, hospital acceptance, emergency support-point inventory or operator restoration ledger.
Past Phase 2, completed/planned projects, dynamic no-outage status and annual visits retain their own time/scope; none is a T+72 forecast.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at all checkpoints, but river, pluvial, wildfire, heat and compound interpretations contain release-blocking local gaps.
notes: The mandated gate exercised severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

River-flood gives 1.200688 m at T+24/T+72; at T+24 severity is 0.374458 with 16,805 affected and Mobility 0.148348, while T+72 remains critical with 18,056 affected and 1,048,382.027 deprived person-hours.

Pluvial-flood gives 0.387026 m, 6,570 affected, Drainage 0.508888 and Mobility 0.452702 at T+24, then zero depth/affected and operational at T+72 without local rainfall, groundwater, sewer, pump, receiving-water or access milestones.

Canonical wildfire gives drought 0.593562 and smoke 0.278520 but zero local flame at T+24. Heat forcing persists at severity 0.080606 through T+72 while the municipality is labelled operational with zero affected.

Compound retains 0.434808 m, 23,370 affected and exactly unchanged eight-service values from T+48 to T+72. Coastal direct depth and remote Groningen earthquake shaking are correctly zero, but only for those named direct screens.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused deterministic contract passes boundedness, causal-ledger closure, population/demand/delivery reconciliation and monotonic cumulative burden.
notes: Initial command MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0824 pnpm audit:model passed one file and two tests.
All values are finite/bounded, affected population is integral and bounded, and all 35 local allocations reconcile to municipality population, demand and delivery.
Passing arithmetic proves implementation invariants, not physical calibration, evidence validity or response readiness.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common seeded surface overrides distinct stream, pluvial, wind, heat, cyber, winter and nature-fire mechanisms and fails a local-source test.
notes: At T+24, severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire have exactly the same full 35-neighbourhood severity order, led by Industriebegied Stokeind, Pannenschuur Centrum and De Lind/Kerkstraat.

A controlled hypothetical wildfire source at the official centre of BU08240401 buitengebied Oisterwijk Zuid [5.232658885488843, 51.56801337326252], used transparently as an Oisterwijkse Bossen-area proxy, gives fire 0.544508, smoke 0.513947 and 7,565 affected but ranks the source neighbourhood only 13th/35 across every service.
The controlled source is not an observed ignition and the label point is not a fuel polygon. The test shows that explicit source distance does not overcome the shared municipal seed.
No watercourse/terrain/stress surface, paved heat field, forest/heath/fen eligibility, fuel/moisture, visitors, barriers, access, wind or suppression field drives allocation.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact eight-service trajectories exceed available stream/RWZI, transport, care, drinking-water, power and telecom evidence.
notes: Forty-nine water points and RWZI Haaren identify assets/design context but not connected topology, current controls/inflow/quality, power dependency, redundancy or repair.

Brabant Water names Haaren/Oirschot sources; one TBN Tilburg Noord capacity sample and Enexis planning pages are not outage/load/switching evidence. Sixty-eight RDI antenna installations are not coverage/backhaul/backup state.

Facilities omits De Hondsberg and external acute-care continuity. Twenty-five DUO education records, including special education and an AZC-school label, are registrations rather than shelter, occupancy or resource evidence.
Mobility/Supply use three logical road proxies; rail, internal routes, crossings, fire/water closures and hospital acceptance do not drive availability.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers reconcile, but their synthetic causal stages omit accountable authority, validity, local mechanisms and physical dependency provenance.
notes: Scenario contributions are visible and exact, but they are model assumptions rather than observations or operator assessments.

The evidence set includes static context, a design programme, future projects, an adopted regional scenario, dated Phase 2, dynamic no-outage status, annual visitor estimates, partial registers and synthetic results; these evidence classes must remain distinct.

No local Waterinfo point/forecast, null asset capacity, absent acute-care site and unknown visitor count remain Unknown/NoData, not zero water, zero assets, safe routes, empty nature or restored services.

recovery72h.summary: First-72-hour degradation and recovery lack incident-specific actions, authorities, prerequisites, resource state and completion evidence.
notes: Compound service values freeze from T+48 to T+72 while 23,370 remain affected and depth remains 0.434808 m, without a blocker or action ledger. River remains critical; pluvial, winter, wildfire and severe storm recover generically without operator milestones.
Heat is still forced through T+72 but status becomes operational and affected becomes zero; this threshold result cannot mean the 26% older population, visitors or institutions need no action.

At T+0-6, select the event and valid window; identify VRMWB/municipality/water-board/land-manager/operator lead; capture stream controls, ignition/perimeter, visitor/institution exposure, warnings and support-point activation. At T+6-24 track rural/forest and N65/A58/rail access, ETZ acceptance, vehicles/crews, vulnerable-person contact, utility and RWZI assessments.

At T+24-72 track shelter/support-point staffing and stock, resupply, welfare, water quality/pressure, sewer/RWZI status, access restoration, fire containment, visitor accounting, controlled return and evidence-backed completion. Missing or expired state must remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, settlements and population reconcile.
findings.evidence: E01-E02 verify GM0824, its contained centre, 33,108 residents, 35 neighbourhoods, four BAG places, 21 BRT settlements, unique safety-region assignment and three NWB border links. Neighbourhood population differs by only three residents (-0.009%).
findings.action: Retain official identity/boundary, independent BAG/BRT roles, transparent three-person reconciliation and field-level null semantics; do not alter rounded source observations.

findings.summary: The river preset publishes unsupported 1.2-metre local inundation without selecting Oisterwijk's connected stream conditions.
findings.evidence: The model gives 1.200688 m at T+24/T+72 and 18,056 affected at T+72. E04 establishes the Voorste and Achterste Stroom joining the Essche Stroom and downstream Dommel connection, but no upstream rain/discharge, downstream level, kade/weir state, breach/overtopping, forecast or depth footprint drives the result.
findings.action: Retain water-system plausibility but suppress the current local depth, affected and hotspot precision as unsupported. Require a governed Voorste/Achterste/Essche/Dommel case with issue/validity, boundary/control/defence state and licensed depth/extent. Do not convert suppression into safety for brook, groundwater, pluvial or drainage pathways.

findings.summary: Exact pluvial depth and automatic recovery ignore municipal rainfall, groundwater, sewer, pump and receiving-water mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 gives 0.387026 m, 6,570 affected, Drainage 0.508888 and Mobility 0.452702; T+72 reports zero depth/affected and operational. E03's >60 mm overflow narrative is a design rule, not a scenario field; E04/E10 identify connected streams and assets but no live state.
findings.action: Ingest versioned municipal/AHN pluvial evidence and bind rainfall/duration, antecedent groundwater, sewer/ditch topology, pump/RWZI state, Voorste/Achterste/Essche receiving levels, road thresholds and dewatering. Until then render local metre/rank/recovery values unsupported.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one complete 35-neighbourhood severity order.
findings.evidence: Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire at T+24 share the full order led by Industriebegied Stokeind, Pannenschuur Centrum and De Lind/Kerkstraat. E03-E08 describe distinct paved, water, forest/heath/fen, visitor, wind and digital mechanisms.
findings.action: Replace the common hash with hazard-specific versioned evidence. Unsupported local maps must render Unknown without numeric hotspot labels; a supported hazard field should then remain invariant only across service views.

findings.summary: Canonical wildfire omits local flame and a controlled Oisterwijkse Bossen-area source fails neighbourhood containment ranking.
findings.evidence: Canonical T+24 gives smoke 0.278520 and drought 0.593562 but fire 0. A hypothetical BU08240401 source gives fire 0.544508, smoke 0.513947 and 7,565 affected, yet its own neighbourhood ranks 13/35. E05-E08 establish heavily visited forest/heath/fen exposure and a dated elevated fire phase but not a live incident.
findings.action: Keep remote smoke as a separately named exercise. Add authoritative combustible-area eligibility, ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid wind, visitor/institution exposure, barriers, roads, water points and suppression; assert containing-eligible-area priority for a controlled GM0824 regression.

findings.summary: Resident-only affected population omits major nature recreation and specialist-care continuity.
findings.evidence: E05 estimates 500,000-800,000 annual visits but explicitly lacks precise central visitor data. E11 identifies nationally serving 24-hour specialist youth care at De Hondsberg. Neither current visitors/clients/staff nor their evacuation, shelter-in-place, medication, transport and continuity needs enter the 33,108-resident allocation.
findings.action: Add separately typed and timestamped transient/institution exposure inputs using land-manager counters, accommodation/operator reports and facility continuity data where lawful. Never force annual estimates or unknown occupancy into residents; show Unknown ranges and privacy-preserving aggregates.

findings.summary: Three road proxies and a station point cannot support N65/A58, rail, stream-crossing or rural evacuation decisions.
findings.evidence: E02 provides two serial A58 edges, a short N65 edge, station Oisterwijk and scheduled stops but no live capacity. E09 locates a pedestrian rail/Essche Stroom tunnel. Internal forest/rural roads, bridges/culverts, closures, train/bus operation, vehicles and ETZ route acceptance are absent.
findings.action: Build a typed multimodal graph with internal roads, N65/A58 access, water/rail crossings, event-valid NDW/ProRail/authority state, vehicle/crew availability and destination-specific hospital acceptance. Do not infer emergency passability from geometry, project completion or schedule presence.

findings.summary: Exact water, drainage, power and telecom trajectories exceed the available public topology and live-state evidence.
findings.evidence: E10 supplies 49 partial water points including RWZI Haaren with missing units/topology/state; E12 names two drinking-water sources and a dated no-outage/power-planning context. One TBN sample and 68 antenna points do not establish municipal coverage, dependencies, reserve or restoration.
findings.action: Keep public points/zones as provenance-rich non-causal context and label exact service percentages synthetic indices. Activate physical propagation only from operator-approved topology/state; unavailable or sensitive pipe, feeder, backhaul and backup detail remains Unknown.

findings.summary: First-72-hour status and recovery lack accountable local action, resource and completion evidence.
findings.evidence: Compound service values freeze from T+48 to T+72 with 23,370 affected and 0.434808 m. Pluvial generically becomes operational; heat remains forced but reports operational/zero affected. E07 and E13 require accountable crisis roles, warnings, support points and vulnerable-person action, none of which drives the curves.
findings.action: For every T+0/6/12/24/48/72 change record authority, action, target, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid times, evidence class, progress and completion. Track fire containment, visitor accounting, institutional continuity, road/rail access, ETZ acceptance, utility/RWZI inspection, support-point activation and resupply.

findings.summary: Missing observations, forecasts, capacities and occupancy can be misread as zero or safe.
findings.evidence: There are no assigned Waterinfo observation/forecast or acute-care points, most weir capacities are null, visitor counts are annual estimates, and current operator pages are snapshots. Twenty-five education records and one station do not prove emergency roles or operation.
findings.action: Expose publisher, edition, observed/issued/valid/retrieved time, coverage, licence and evidence class per field. Render Unknown/NoData explicitly and keep it numerically neutral; never convert it to zero, safe, empty, closed, unavailable or restored.

corrections.summary: Make GM0824 river output conditional on a governed Voorste/Achterste/Essche Stroom and downstream Dommel hydraulic scenario.
corrections.validation: Without selected boundary/control/defence/footprint evidence, keep amplitude diagnostic only, mark spatialEvidence unsupported and render local depth/affected/hotspots Unknown; verify local brook/pluvial/groundwater risk remains unresolved rather than safe.

corrections.validation: Verify publisher, edition, rainfall duration, depth units, licence and NoData; reproduce official stress mechanisms and require groundwater, receiving-level, pump/RWZI and road-threshold validity before calculating Drainage or recovery.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific evidence and a source-aware Oisterwijkse Bossen/Kampina fire adapter.
corrections.validation: Eight unrelated hazards must not share one full rank; a controlled BU08240401 eligible-area source must prioritize its containing area; remote smoke remains separately labelled and unsupported maps render Unknown.

corrections.summary: Add privacy-preserving transient visitor and specialist-care exposure without merging it into CBS residents.
corrections.validation: Display residents, dated visitor estimates/counters and institution occupancy ranges separately; unknown event-hour presence remains Unknown; require facility/land-manager validity before evacuation or welfare demand is computed.

corrections.summary: Build typed N65/A58/rail/rural access and external-care context without inventing operation or capacity.
corrections.validation: Verify serial A58 identity, N65 access, internal forest roads, stream/rail crossings, Oisterwijk station and ETZ destination; require valid closure/passability, vehicle/crew, rail/bus operation and hospital acceptance before asserting reachability.

corrections.summary: Keep water, drinking-water, power and telecom records provenance-rich and non-causal until operator-approved topology/state is available.
corrections.validation: Registers expose publisher, edition, retrieval/validity, coverage, licence and evidence class; null units/topology and one-sample coverage remain Unknown; current no-outage does not project through T+72 or change synthetic service values.

corrections.summary: Bind every GM0824 first-72-hour service and recovery transition to accountable actions and resources.
corrections.validation: Snapshot T+0/6/12/24/48/72 authority, action, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid time, evidence class, progress and completion; reject operational/restored labels without evidence and show thresholded residents beside transient/institution uncertainty and residual pressure.

residualLimitations: No event-valid Voorste/Achterste/Essche Stroom or downstream Dommel boundary, defence/control state, inundation footprint or forecast is causally consumed.

No versioned municipal pluvial raster, AHN flow path, antecedent groundwater, sewer/ditch topology, pump/RWZI state, receiving level, road threshold or dewatering state is connected to the exercise clock.
Municipal >60 mm overflow language is design context, not observed capacity, a selected rainfall event or proof of performance.
